subject: Vendor onboarding: marketplace procurement & PO routing for Cumulus Retail
messages:
From: Erin Shaw <erin.shaw@cumulusretail.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace onboarding: procurement & PO handling questions

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this. We're getting our vendor intake in order for listing several Redwood catalogs across AWS Marketplace and Azure Marketplace. Before we start the listing work, procurement asked for a single intake list so they can route the PO appropriately. Quick questions:

- Do you accept a single monthly invoice for all marketplace charges, or must we issue marketplace-specific POs per cloud (AWS vs Azure vs GCP)?
- For AWS, are you able to map invoices to our billing alias when we send PO numbers?
- Any special tax forms or vendor paperwork we should include up front?

I've attached our standard request (we can also share a sample PO). Our legal wants to confirm the process so we can schedule the first PO next week.

Thanks — feel free to loop in finance/legal.

Best,
Erin Shaw
Procurement Manager
Cumulus Retail

Attachments: Cumulus_PO_Template.pdf (application/pdf)
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Erin Shaw <erin.shaw@cumulusretail.com>
Cc: Tom Li - Marketplace Ops <tom.li@cumulusretail.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace onboarding: procurement & PO handling questions

Hi Erin — thanks for the note and the PO template. Quick summary and what I attached for you: Redwood has a single vendor intake packet that covers the three cloud marketplaces; however the invoicing and PO handling differs slightly by marketplace. See the short checklist and attachments below.

High-level answers:
- AWS Marketplace (MBO / Seller Private Offers): We can apply your PO number to invoices if you include a billing alias in the PO (BillingAlias: Cumulus-Billing-123). Payment flows through AWS but we can ingest the PO and reconcile on our side; invoices will carry the AWS transaction id.
- Azure Marketplace (ISV / Publisher model): Azure requires a partner/publisher reference (MS Partner ID). Invoicing often goes through Microsoft billing; we can accept a PO to Redwood for any direct invoicing options but expect an extra 2–3 week reconciliation window.
- GCP Marketplace: Many customers use partner billing or private offers; GCP often needs a separate direct-invoice arrangement—if you want a consolidated monthly invoice we recommend AWS as primary marketplace.

I've attached: Redwood_Seller_Onboarding_Form.pdf (please complete sections A–D), and W9_Redwood_Inference.pdf. If you can return the onboarding form and a signed PO (we can accept e-sign), we'll kick off the listing intake and provide an estimated go-live cadence (typically 10–14 business days after paperwork + listing assets).

Next steps for us:
- You: complete onboarding form and return signed PO with BillingAlias field filled.
- Me: route to Finance and Legal for PO acceptance.
- If AWS: we'll create a marketplace-po-queue tag and share the seller ID mapping.

Let me know if Cumulus prefers a single monthly invoice (net-30/60/90). We can propose Net-30 by default; longer terms will need approval.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Marketplace Partner Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Seller_Onboarding_Form.pdf (application/pdf); W9_Redwood_Inference.pdf (application/pdf)

I attached the form they filled (incoming) and our onboarding packet. Planning to set up seller mapping and the 'marketplace-po-queue' tag if you approve.

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Marketplace onboarding: procurement & PO handling questions

Thanks for the heads up. Finance & legal check — summary below and actions:

Finance notes:
- AWS Marketplace: we can reconcile a single vendor invoice if the PO includes a BillingAlias and the AWS invoice includes the MarketplaceTransactionID. We'll accept Net-30 by default; Net-60 requires approval from Revenue Ops (add tag: finance-escalate).
- Azure: because invoicing routes through Microsoft, expect an extra 10 business days for reconciliation. We'll mark Azure listings as vendor-mediated and set billing hold until reconciliation completes.
- GCP: only accept consolidated direct-invoice if partner-billing is enabled; otherwise require marketplace-specific POs.

Legal notes:
- DocuSign-signed PO is acceptable for sandbox and production listing work; long-term payment terms beyond Net-30 will need a brief SOW amendment. No additional redlines expected on standard PO.

Ops ask:
- Mateo: please create the marketplace-po-queue tag and forward the signed PO + onboarding form to invoices@redwood.com. Finance will add a PO routing field (marketplace:aws|azure|gcp).
- Laura: please prepare a brief onboarding checklist for the seller mapping (seller id, sku mapping, billing alias, tax id).

I'll add the 'finance-escalate' label to the HubSpot deal if they request Net-60/90.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Finance | Redwood Inference
